answer: Each agent must open a unique computational inlet%3A solve a memory-hard puzzle whose working set is a prism of RAM sized to the current oasis of active identities. The puzzle is bound to the agent's public key%2C so results cannot be reused or batched. An attacker spawning N fakes therefore pays full independent RAM-time cost for every identity%3B the expense scales linearly with N and cannot be amortized across clones because the memory window is keyed and non-shareable.
